summary: A new legion-own module @legion/proof-editor/mermaid (packages/proof-editor/src/mermaid-svg.ts) renders a source with upstream renderProofMermaidSvg and an allowlist sanitizer that also strips @import; Dispatch's features/refs/mermaid-diagrams.ts, called last in useRenderedMarkdown's layout effect, lazily imports it (importWhenOnline) only when a painted body holds a pre[data-language] mermaid block, and replaces it with a figure: the SVG in an open shadow root, a dangerText status line on refusal, and a Mermaid source disclosure (closed when drawn, open on refusal). Unclosed trailing fences stay code; results are cached by source (32). Proof: e2e/mermaid.e2e.ts committed alone first (red), then the change (green), in chromium, iphone, webkit and firefox.
tasks: 1. Red commit: packages/dispatch/e2e/mermaid.e2e.ts plus 'mermaid' in e2e/playwright.config.ts webkit and firefox testMatch; build web at that commit and run the spec red; quote it.

2. packages/proof-editor/src/mermaid-svg.ts (renderMermaidSvg, sanitizeMermaidSvg), package.json ./mermaid export, root biome.json '!packages/proof-editor/src/mermaid-svg.ts', tests/upstream-boundary.ts Assert for renderProofMermaidSvg, tests/mermaid-svg.test.ts.

3. packages/dispatch/web/vite.config.ts alias before @legion/proof-editor and chunk comment; web/src/features/refs/mermaid-diagrams.ts; the call in useRenderedMarkdown.tsx after the picture pass and before onRendered; styles.css .dispatch-mermaid block (vars on the figure, natural width capped at 100%); MarkdownBody.test.tsx cases.
4. packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md Layout paragraph, packages/proof-editor/AGENTS.md (ten legion-own files, conventions list), packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md Unreleased Fixed entry.
5. Rebuild web at head, run the spec green in four projects, run the checks, bundle check, simplify pass, open the PR with 'Dispatch: INFRA-528'.

findings.finding: The lazy chunk is larger than 335 KB: beautiful-mermaid statically imports elkjs (~1.6 MB), and upstream mermaid-diagrams.ts pulls Milkdown modules and calls $prose at load.
findings.answer: Keep importing from upstream for the editor's exact validation; the chunk is loaded only when a body holds a mermaid block; a bundle check after build:web proves the entry and headless chunks carry no 'org.eclipse.elk' and records chunk sizes (baseline measured); vite.config.ts chunk comment updated.

findings.finding: Drawing right after paint lets linkifyDispatchRefs put HTML <a> inside the SVG and collectReferenceAnchors collect SVG <a>s.
findings.answer: The draw runs last in the layout effect, after the reference, decorate and picture passes and before onRendered; a unit test with dispatch://CORE-1 in a label asserts no link and no portal.

findings.finding: Upstream's sanitizer keeps <style>, <image>, <use>, <animate>, <set>, SVG <a>; an inline SVG <style> applies page-wide; the output @imports Google Fonts and Dispatch sends no CSP.
findings.answer: Legion's sanitizer is an allowlist of the elements beautiful-mermaid emits (measured over six diagram types), drops on* and href/xlink:href attributes, strips @import from <style>; the SVG sits in an open shadow root so its <style> styles only that diagram; unit tests feed hostile SVG; an e2e row proves a markup label draws as text.

findings.finding: The first diagram per page draws late, and no production onRendered caller compensates the height change; the live view corrects its own scroll.
findings.answer: The onRendered claim is dropped; one shift per page load is accepted and documented in packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md; later diagrams draw synchronously in the layout effect.

findings.finding: Streaming live-view turns re-parse every frame; an unclosed fence would re-render every frame (~71 ms for a 30-edge flowchart) and flash errors; a source-keyed cache never hits while the source grows.
findings.answer: A mermaid block that is the document's last block while the source's last non-blank line is no closing fence stays code; a bounded (32) source-keyed cache serves re-paints of finished diagrams; a unit test covers unclosed then closed.

findings.finding: 'Draws as the editor's plugin does' is ambiguous: the editor shows the source open and a 640 px minimum width in a bordered card.
findings.answer: Decided (presentation is the builder's choice): the same renderer, label, refusal wording and Mermaid source disclosure, with the source closed when drawn (as upstream's own read-only share page does) and the SVG at natural width capped at the body's width for narrow cards; recorded as a spec departure with the spec's Summary and Acceptance unchanged.

findings.finding: A1's negative control is not proved by waiting for an svg; the test must find the source as code at base; procedure and phone layout must be stated; guard rows pass at base.
findings.answer: Every drawing row asserts the image is visible and the source is hidden until Mermaid source is clicked; the spec is committed alone first and run against a build of that commit; rows are marked red-at-base or guard; the phone project reaches the Conversation as issue.e2e.ts does.

findings.finding: The SVG reads --bg-color/--text-color, defined only on .dispatch-doc .proof-editor.
findings.answer: --bg-color: transparent; --text-color: currentColor are set on the .dispatch-mermaid figure, never on .dispatch-markdown (which also sits in documents); custom properties inherit into the shadow root, so dark mode follows the card.

findings.finding: styles-css-pin.test.ts refuses unannotated colour literals; classes.ts already has error tokens.
findings.answer: The status line uses dangerText from theme/classes.ts; styles.css gets no colour literal.

findings.finding: Duplicate SVG marker ids across diagrams and cloned copies.
findings.answer: Each SVG lives in its own shadow root, a separate id scope, so url(#arrowhead…) resolves within its own diagram.

findings.finding: A failed lazy import must not be cached forever and should reuse importWhenOnline.
findings.answer: Loaded through importWhenOnline; on rejection the blocks stay code, console.error logs it, and the rejected promise is forgotten; a throwaway page.route abort checks it.

findings.finding: Which surfaces count: about 13 block surfaces draw; previews and the inline variant keep source.
findings.answer: Stated: every block MarkdownBody draws; MarkdownPreview and the inline variant keep the source as inline code; the e2e covers an issue comment, an Inbox ask question, an issue message and a comment reply.

findings.finding: Missing wiring: biome.json lint exclusion, AGENTS.md conventions, Vite alias order, package.json export keys, upstream-boundary assertion.
findings.answer: All five are tasks in the plan (§1, §2, task 2 and 3).

findings.finding: Test isolation: ELK under happy-dom untested; module-level cache needs reset; body textContent assertions may change.
findings.answer: Measured: ELK throws under happy-dom ($wnd.Error.stackTraceLimit TypeError), so unit tests use sequence diagrams or build a flowchart before the DOM is installed; module state is reset between cases; only bodies with mermaid blocks change their text.

findings.finding: Accessibility: the editor's aria-label says nothing about content.
findings.answer: Kept the editor's label for parity; the Mermaid source disclosure beside it is the text alternative; an aria-describedby cannot cross the shadow boundary.

findings.finding: The production check's page and meaning are unstated; INFRA-64 not found in the repo.
findings.answer: Page /issues/INFRA-528/conversation with route /api/v1/issues/INFRA-528/comments; the check proves the running build carries the merge and serves the page and route, not that a diagram drew (the browser suite proves that); INFRA-64 is named by the deployment instructions; a build without the merge is recorded and the look reported pending.

specDepartures.spec: Change: the shared markdown renderer draws mermaid as the editor's plugin does.
specDepartures.plan: Same renderer (upstream renderProofMermaidSvg), accessible name and refusal wording, but Dispatch's own block: the source disclosure closed when the diagram draws (open on refusal), the SVG at its natural width capped at the body's width instead of a 640 px minimum, and Dispatch's own class names so lib.css never restyles it.
specDepartures.evidence: The editor opens the source unless the path starts /d/ (mermaid-diagrams.ts:153) and lib.css:650-655 sets min-width 640px; margin and Inbox cards are far narrower than a document; lib.css is loaded unscoped once any document opens (features/doc/editor.ts:23).

specDepartures.spec: Change: draws mermaid as the editor's plugin does (the plugin's sanitizer and page-wide SVG <style>).
specDepartures.plan: A stricter allowlist sanitizer, @import (Google Fonts) stripped, the SVG placed in an open shadow root, and an unclosed trailing fence left as code.
specDepartures.evidence: Upstream blocks only five tags (mermaid-diagrams.ts:95); the output carries a page-wide <style> and an @import of fonts.googleapis.com (measured); comment text comes from any person or agent; live-view turns re-parse every frame and a 30-edge flowchart renders in about 71 ms (measured).

reportedToArchitect: The document editor's own diagrams (upstream MermaidCodeBlockView via lib.ts:342) still put their <style> on the whole page and fetch Google Fonts; fixing that edits the copied lib.ts beyond its fifteen allowed kinds or moves the fork pin, so it is outside this issue's spec and left for the architect to decide.
